content: 1. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir itself and cyclosporine by altering the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Danazol increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of daridorexant through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. The dose of daridorexant should not exceed 25 mg per night when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 5. Darifenacin increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir, and fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of darifenacin, both through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 6. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Dasatinib increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 8. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of deflazacort via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. The deflazacort dose should be reduced to one-third of the recommended dose when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Fosamprenavir increases desvenlafaxine levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are required. 11. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone, while dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir, both via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Herbal DHEA increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 14. Fosamprenavir increases diazepam levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing adverse reactions. Therapy modification, close monitoring, and alternative options are recommended. 15. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of diazoxide, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 16. Didanosine decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies to oral forms of both agents. Didanosine should be administered two hours before or several hours after fosamprenavir. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in plasma estrogen and progestin levels have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors. Monitoring for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache is recommended. 18. Diltiazem increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Protease inhibitors may decrease diltiazem metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 19. Fosamprenavir increases dofetilide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity and the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Therapy modification, close monitoring, and alternative options are recommended. 20. Fosamprenavir increases doravirine levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 21. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin and its liposomal form via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Fosamprenavir increases dronabinol levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 23. Dronedarone increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 24. Efavirenz decreases fosamprenavir levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Elagolix decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 26. Fosamprenavir increases eletriptan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 27. Eliglustat increases fosamprenavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 28. Fosamprenavir increases elvitegravir levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 29. Fosamprenavir and emtricitabine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Encorafenib affects fosamprenavir levels by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Fosamprenavir increases erlotinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 32. Fosamprenavir increases escitalopram levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. Caution and monitoring are required. 33. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases fosamprenavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 34. Esomeprazole decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Fosamprenavir increases estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 36. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal, conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 37. Fosamprenavir increases eszopiclone levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended, with a reduced starting dose of 1 mg/day for eszopiclone. 38. Fosamprenavir increases ethosuximide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are required. 39. Fosamprenavir increases etonogestrel levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 40. Fosamprenavir increases etoposide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Fosamprenavir increases etravirine levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 42. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution and suspension, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are required. 43. Famotidine decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Fedratinib increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments for CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Fosamprenavir increases felodipine levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 46. Fosamprenavir increases fesoterodine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 47. Fosamprenavir increases finerenone levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised, with serum potassium monitoring during initiation and dosage adjustment. 48. Fluconazole increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 49. Fosamprenavir increases fludrocortisone levels, while fludrocortisone decreases fosamprenavir levels, both via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 50. Fosamprenavir increases flurazepam levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification, close monitoring, and alternative options are recommended. 51. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 52. Fluvoxamine increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 53. Fosaprepitant increases fosamprenavir levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 54. Fosphenytoin affects fosamprenavir levels, with variable effects depending on co-administration with ritonavir. Caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Fosamprenavir increases fostamatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 56. Garlic decreases fosamprenavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 57. Fosamprenavir increases gefitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing adverse effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 58. Fosamprenavir increases gepirone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, with both drugs increasing the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 59. Fosamprenavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 60. Fosamprenavir decreases glimepiride effects, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are required. 61. Fosamprenavir affects glipizide levels variably, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 62. Fosamprenavir decreases glyburide effects, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are required. 63. Grapefruit increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 64. Griseofulvin decreases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 65. Fosamprenavir increases guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended, with dosage adjustments for extended-release guanfacine. 66. Fosamprenavir increases hydrocodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 67. Fosamprenavir increases hydrocortisone levels, while hydrocortisone decreases fosamprenavir levels, both via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 68. Fosamprenavir increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 69. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 70. Fosamprenavir decreases ifosfamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing its effectiveness. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 71. Fosamprenavir increases iloperidone levels, while iloperidone increases fosamprenavir levels, both via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 72. Fosamprenavir increases imipramine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 73. Fosamprenavir increases indinavir levels, while indinavir increases fosamprenavir levels, both via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 74. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of various insulin formulations (e.g., aspart, degludec, detemir, glargine, glulisine, inhaled, lispro, NPH, and regular human insulin) due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 75. Fosamprenavir decreases isavuconazonium sulfate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 76. Isoniazid increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 77. Istradefylline increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 78. Fosamprenavir increases ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised, with dose adjustments for ivacaftor. 79. Fosamprenavir increases ixabepilone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 80. Fosamprenavir decreases ketamine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 81. Fosamprenavir increases lacosamide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 82. Fosamprenavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 83. Lansoprazole decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 84. Fosamprenavir increases lapatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 85. Fosamprenavir increases larotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 86. Fosamprenavir increases lefamulin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring for adverse effects is recommended. 87. Lenacapavir increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 88. Fosamprenavir increases levamlodipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 89. Fosamprenavir increases levomilnacipran levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised, with a maximum dose of 80 mg/day for levomilnacipran. 90. Fosamprenavir increases levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended. 91. Fosamprenavir decreases linagliptin effects, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are required. 92. Fosamprenavir decreases liraglutide effects, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 93. Lomitapide increases fosamprenavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 94. Fosamprenavir increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 95. Fosamprenavir increases loratadine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 96. Fosamprenavir increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised.
